transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm answering this right, but... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit. It's really nothing too terrible, I promise, just... I guess I've been doing some odd little things at church lately. 

Like, well, I help out at the potluck table, and sometimes I'll just... stand there. I'll be holding the serving spoon up in the air, and I just don't move at all. Or I'll catch myself folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over again, right while folks are standing there waiting on me to finish. I feel so bad holding up the line, and I don't mean to be a bother to anyone. I'm trying to do better with it, I really am. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.

When you notice yourself repeating the napkin folding or freezing with the spoon, do you feel a strong urge or anxious pressure inside you that makes you do it, or does it just happen without you feeling like you're choosing to do it?

Oh, well... I don't think I feel any kind of anxious pressure, no. Nothing like that. It's not a strong urge or anything bad. It just... I suppose it just happens without me really deciding to do it. 

Like I just sort of drift off for a little second, and my hands either stop moving or they just keep doing the exact same thing. I don't feel upset inside when it happens, I promise. It's just a silly little habit, really, nothing to fuss over too much. I just feel awful bad when I realize folks are waiting on me and I'm being a nuisance. 

Does... does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.

Have you noticed or experienced anything unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others have told you seem unusual or hard to believe?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that at all. I mean... I know some folks get a little confused as they get older, but my mind is still sharp as a tack, thank the Lord. 

I don't hear anything that isn't there, and I certainly don't have any strange ideas. I just go to church, tend to my little garden, and try to be a good neighbor. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my wits or anything terrible like that. I'm just a regular old lady who gets a bit stuck sometimes when she's serving the casserole. 

Is... is it okay that I don't have those things happening? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you can do your job properly.
Have you had any recent medical problems, illnesses, head injuries, or new medications that started around the same time you began noticing these episodes of freezing or repeating movements?

Oh, no, Doctor, nothing like that. My health has been just fine, really. I haven't been sick, and I certainly haven't hit my head or anything clumsy like that. I'm very careful on my feet, you know. 

And as for medicines, well, I just take my regular little pills for my blood pressure, the same ones I've been on for years and years. Nothing new at all. I wouldn't want to go messing with my routine and cause any trouble. 

So, no, there's no big medical problem causing this, I'm quite sure of it. I'm generally a very healthy person, I try to take good care of myself so I don't become a burden to anyone. I hope that's a good thing, Doctor? I know you have to check all these things to be thorough.

Besides the freezing and repetitive folding, have you or anyone else noticed other unusual body movements or postures, like your body staying in an unusual position someone else places it in, or times when you don't speak at all for a while?

Oh my, no. Nothing strange like that. Nobody has ever had to... to pose me like a doll or anything. I move my own arms and legs just fine, thank goodness. 

And as for not speaking, well... I'm always happy to pass the time of day with folks. My neighbor says I'm quite the chatterbox when I get going about my garden. I'd never just sit there refusing to answer someone, that would be terribly rude, wouldn't it? I was raised to always be polite and answer when spoken to. 

It's really just those little pauses we talked about, nothing more than that. I hope it's alright that I don't have those other things you mentioned? I really am trying my best to be a good patient for you, Doctor. Am I doing okay with your questions?
When someone tries to gently move your arm or guide you while you're in one of these episodes, do you find yourself resisting or pushing against them without meaning to?

Oh, heavens, no. I would never push or fight against anyone. That sounds so... well, so stubborn and impolite, doesn't it? 

If someone, like my dear neighbor, gently touches my arm when I'm having one of my little pauses, I don't resist at all. I wouldn't dream of being difficult. I just sort of... stay right there. I don't push back or try to wrestle away, I promise you that. I've always prided myself on being agreeable and easy to get along with. 

I'd hate for anyone to think I was being a nuisance or causing trouble when they're just trying to help an old lady. I hope that's the right answer, Doctor? I really don't want you to think poorly of me. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can be.
Have you or your family noticed any recent changes in your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations, misplacing things more than usual, or getting confused about dates or places?

Oh, goodness, no. My memory is just as sharp as a tack, Doctor. I really haven't had any trouble with that at all. 

I mean, everyone misplaces their reading glasses now and then, don't they? But nothing out of the ordinary, certainly nothing like forgetting conversations or getting all muddled up about what day it is. I keep my calendar right by the telephone and check it every morning, so I always know exactly where I'm supposed to be. 

I wouldn't want you to think my mind is slipping away from me. I'm still very capable of managing my own affairs, truly I am. It's just those little pauses we talked about, nothing wrong with my memory. I hope that's reassuring to hear? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or uninterested in things you normally enjoy, or on the other hand, unusually elated or full of energy, over the past few weeks?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that at all. I've been in very good spirits, Doctor, very good indeed. 

I still love tending to my garden, and I always look forward to my afternoon tea. I certainly haven't been feeling sad or down in the dumps... and I haven't been running around like a headless chicken with too much energy, either! I'm just my usual, steady self. I like to keep things calm and pleasant, you know? 

I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm becoming depressed or... or overly excitable. I'm keeping quite a nice, even keel. Is that what you were hoping to hear? I do want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how well I'm doing.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any neurological conditions, such as Parkinson's disease, seizures, or a stroke, or noticed any tremors or stiffness in your body?

Oh, my, no. I've never had any of those terrible things. No strokes or... or seizures, thank the Lord. I've always been told I have a very strong constitution. 

And no shaking or stiffness, either. I mean, my knees get just a tiny bit creaky when I first get out of bed, but that's just from being seventy-one, isn't it? My hands are as steady as can be. I can still pour my afternoon tea without spilling a single drop, and I certainly don't have that Parkinson's disease. 

I've never had to see a special nerve doctor or anything like that. I try very hard to take good care of my physical health so I don't become a worry to anybody. That's a good sign, isn't it, Doctor? I'm doing my best to stay in tip-top shape for you.
Can you tell me approximately when these freezing and repeating episodes first started, and how long each episode usually lasts?

Well... let me think. I suppose it hasn't been terribly long. Maybe... oh, about the past six months or so? That's when folks started mentioning that I was being a little... well, a little hard to follow when I talk, or doing little odd things. 

But it's really nothing major, I promise you! When those little freezing moments happen, they only last a very short time. Just a minute or two, maybe even less, and then I'm right back to my old self. I just sort of... catch my breath and start again. 

I hope that doesn't sound too awful, Doctor. I really do try my very best to speak clearly and behave properly so I don't bother anyone. Am I making sense to you today? I want to be absolutely sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.

You mentioned that folks said you were sometimes 'hard to follow' when you talk—can you tell me more about that? For example, do you lose your train of thought, repeat the same words or phrases, or have trouble finding the right words?

Oh, it's... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, if I'm being honest. I don't want you to think I'm foolish, Doctor. It's really nothing to fret over too much! 

It's just... well, sometimes when the ladies ask me about things, like the charity blankets or choir practice, I fully mean to answer them straight. I really do try to be proper. But then... my words just sort of run off on me. I'll start out fine, and the next thing I know I'm talking about green beans, and then the hymns, and then my roses... and folks just look at me like they can't find what I'm saying at all. 

I don't mean to confuse anyone, I promise. I just get a little tangled up sometimes, and my thoughts just want to visit everything at once. I hope that doesn't make me a bother to people. Am I explaining that alright for you, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and being helpful.
Have you noticed any recent changes like feeling unusually cold, constipation, dry skin, or unexplained weight gain?

Oh, goodness me, no. I haven't had any trouble with any of that at all. I try to be very careful about my health, you see. I always keep my little cardigan handy so I don't catch a chill, and my... well, my bathroom habits are just as regular as can be, thank the Lord. I certainly wouldn't want to be a nuisance to anyone with that sort of trouble. 

And my skin is just normal for a lady my age, I suppose. I always make sure to put a little lotion on so it stays nice. As for my weight, oh, I haven't put on an extra ounce! I try very hard to eat sensible meals so I can stay neat and presentable. 

I'm doing everything I'm supposed to do to take good care of myself. That's a good thing, isn't it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you today and not causing any extra worry.

During one of these freezing spells, if someone were to call your name or ask you a question, are you aware of what's going on around you and able to hear them, even if you can't move or respond right away?

Oh, dear... well, I'm not entirely sure about that, to be perfectly honest. I hope it's alright that I don't quite know. It's just... when I have those little pauses, it's almost like I'm just... tucked away somewhere for a second. I don't really hear folks calling my name or asking things. 

It's certainly not that I'm ignoring anyone, I promise you! I would never, ever want to be rude like that to my friends or neighbors. It's just that I don't seem to notice much of anything at all until I sort of... wake back up to the room. 

I hope that's not a terrible answer, Doctor. I really am trying my best to remember exactly how it happens so I can be helpful to you. Am I doing okay with all these questions?
During these freezing spells, have you or anyone else noticed your face making unusual expressions or grimaces that you weren't intending?

Oh, heavens, no! I certainly hope not. Goodness, that would be so unladylike, wouldn't it? I always try to keep a pleasant expression so people know I'm happy to see them. 

None of the ladies at church or my neighbors have ever mentioned anything like that to me. I would be just mortified if I was pulling faces at people without meaning to! I really do try to be so careful about how I present myself. 

So, no, I haven't noticed anything like that, and no one has said a word about it to me. I'm keeping everything nice and proper, just like I should be. Is that... is that the right sort of thing to be looking out for, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Right before one of these episodes starts, do you ever notice any warning signs, like a strange smell, taste, or feeling of déjà vu, or do they seem to come on with no warning at all?

Oh, no, Doctor. I haven't noticed anything peculiar like that at all. No strange smells or... or funny tastes. I always keep a very clean house, you see, so I'd certainly notice if something smelled off! And I don't get that... that other feeling you mentioned. 

They just seem to... well, they just happen, out of the blue, I suppose. I don't get any warning at all. I hope that's not unhelpful of me to say. I really wish I could give you a better clue about when they're going to happen so we could figure this out. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I'm trying my very best to give you the answers you need, I just don't want to make up a story if it isn't true. I hope I'm still being helpful.
After one of these episodes ends, do you feel confused, unusually tired, or have trouble remembering what just happened, or do you feel completely normal right away?

Oh, my... no, I don't think I feel that way at all. I feel just fine right after, really I do. I certainly wouldn't want to be a bother to anyone by being all mixed up or... or needing to lie down in the middle of the day. Goodness, a lady shouldn't be sleeping the day away! 

I just... well, I just go right back to whatever I was doing before, like it never even happened. I feel completely normal right away, clear as a bell. 

I hope that's a good sign, Doctor? I'm so hoping I'm not making things difficult for you by not having all these extra troubles you're asking about. Am I doing alright with my answers?
During these freezing episodes, have you or anyone else noticed you making small repetitive movements like lip-smacking, chewing, swallowing, or fumbling with your hands or clothing?

Oh, my stars, no. I... I certainly hope I don't do anything like that. Smacking my lips or chewing on nothing... well, my mother always taught me much better manners than that! And I always try to keep my hands folded nicely in my lap, so I wouldn't be fussing or fumbling with my clothes, either. 

None of my friends have ever said a word about me doing anything so... unseemly. I think they would tell me, don't you? I would just be so embarrassed if I was carrying on like that in front of people.

So, no, nothing like that at all. I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to these things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes, Doctor. Am I doing a good job answering your questions?
About how many of these freezing or repeating episodes would you say happen in a typical day?

Oh, goodness... well, I don't really know, Doctor. I haven't been keeping a tally or anything like that. I'm so sorry, I know I should be paying better attention to these things for you. 

I don't think it's very many, really. Just... here and there, I suppose. It certainly doesn't happen all day long, I promise you that. I still get all my chores done and keep the house tidy. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around freezing up all day! 

Is it alright that I don't have an exact number for you? I could try to start counting them if you'd like... I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.

Oh, dear... I don't think you actually asked a question just now, Doctor. Did I miss it? I'm so sorry if I wasn't listening properly, my mind just wanders a bit sometimes. 

I'm trying so hard to be helpful... did you want to ask me something else? I'm ready whenever you are, I promise. I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right for you.

Have you noticed whether these freezing or repeating episodes tend to happen more often when you're feeling stressed, upset, or emotionally overwhelmed, or do they seem to occur regardless of your mood or situation?

Oh, goodness, I... I try very hard not to get upset or overwhelmed, Doctor. I really do try to keep a cheerful disposition and not let things bother me too much. So I wouldn't say they happen because I'm stressed or anything like that. They just sort of... well, they just happen whenever, I suppose, no matter what kind of mood I'm in. 

I hope that's an alright answer? I know it would probably be much more helpful for your notes if I could tell you exactly what sets them off, like being upset. I'm so sorry I don't have a better pattern to give you. Am I still being helpful, even if I don't know the exact cause?
